title: Enterprise Onboarding + Escalation + Integration + QBR Playbook
author: Priya Menon
content:
Summary
-------
This document combines the canonical playbooks used by Customer Success (CS), Support, and Solutions Engineering for enterprise onboarding, integration, escalation handling, and quarterly business review (QBR) preparation. It is intended for CS Managers, Support Engineers, Solutions Engineers, and the SRE/Platform teams supporting customer production workloads.

Scope
-----
- Applies to all enterprise customers (Dedicated and Private customers plus strategic Hosted customers with SLA add-ons).
- Covers: onboarding checklist, integration guide, escalation routing & runbook, known issues & workarounds, monthly health checks and QBR artifact templates.

Ownership and SLAs
------------------
- Document owner: Customer Success (Priya Menon)
- Primary responders: Support (P1/P2), Solutions Engineering (integration), SRE (infrastructure incidents)
- Escalation SLOs (target internal response time):
  1. P1 (production outage / data loss): 15 minutes initial response, 1 hour mitigation plan.
  2. P2 (severe degradation / high error rate): 30 minutes initial response, 4 hour mitigation plan.
  3. P3 (functional but degraded / questions): 4 business hours initial response.

Onboarding checklist (high level)
--------------------------------
1. Contract and access
   - Confirm contract, signal desktop owner, and legal/compliance requirements (DPA, SOC2 addenda).
   - Provision organization and API keys in Redwood Console. Use least-privilege keys for first-stage integration.
2. Network & Security validation
   - For Dedicated/Private: collect VPC subnet, firewall rules, KMS/HSM identifiers, and outbound proxy settings.
   - For Hosted: confirm allowed IP ranges and webhooks endpoints.
3. Dataflows and privacy
   - Confirm data residency and retention requirements. Record in customer onboarding doc.
4. Test harness and performance baseline
   - Run canonical performance suite (link to: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite). Capture throughput, median p95 latency, and token costs.
5. Integration plan and milestones
   - Define integration milestones, success criteria, and owners. Typical 8-week timeline for complex integrations.
6. Go-live checklist
   - Canary rollout plan, monitoring/SLOs, rollback steps, and communication playbook.

Integration guide (developer-facing, condensed)
------------------------------------------------
Pre-reqs
- API keys, model selection, region/endpoint, and network/firewall confirmed.
- SDKs: recommend latest Redwood SDK (v2.x) or REST.

Quick start (example)
- API call (cURL):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.inference/v1/generate \
    -H 'Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>' \
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
    -d '{"model":"redwood-3b","input":"Summarize the following...","max_tokens":256}'

Recommended config by workload
| Workload | Model class | Latency target | Suggested batch size | Notes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Low-latency chat | conversational-llm | <200ms p50 | 1-4 | Enable streaming and short context caching |
| Embeddings (batch) | embedding-enc | N/A | 64-512 | Use bulk endpoint, prefer quantized models for cost |
| Reranking | reranker-v1 | 200-500ms p50 | 16-64 | Consider model distillation for throughput |

Integration test matrix (minimal)
1. Auth: validate token rotation and error handling (401, 403).
2. Rate limiting: validate 429 handling and backoff.
3. Latency and throughput: run load tests matching production patterns.
4. Output stability: snapshot prompts and outputs for regression checks.

Escalation playbook (operational)
----------------------------------
Escalation levels and ownership
- Level 0: Customer -> Support (Triage agent)
- Level 1: Support -> Customer Success / Solutions Engineering (owner for case)
- Level 2: Solutions Engineering -> Eng-SRE / Serving Runtime (for infrastructure/bug)
- Level 3: Exec escalation -> VP CS / CTO / Legal (contract/regulatory impact)

Escalation steps (numbered)
1. Triage: Support assigns severity and documents reproducible steps. Use support template and attach logs/traces.
2. Notify: P1/P2 cases must notify on-call SRE via PagerDuty and create an internal Slack incident channel #incident-<customer>-<id>. Include runbook link.
3. Mitigate: Implement short-term mitigation (traffic reroute to fallback model, increase capacity, disable feature).
4. Postmortem: For P1/P2 outage, SRE + Support + CS must produce a postmortem within 5 business days with RCA and action items.

Escalation contact matrix (short)
- Support on-call: support-oncall@redwood.com, PagerDuty (team: support)
- SRE on-call: sre-oncall@redwood.com, PagerDuty (team: sre)
- Solutions Engineering (work hours): se-team@redwood.com
- Customer Success lead: priya.menon@redwood.com

Known issues and workarounds (living list)
- Issue: Elevated p95 latency for long-sequence requests on quantized kernels.
  Workaround: Pin to non-quantized variant or reduce request context window; limit streaming to core tokens.
- Issue: Token accounting discrepancy for batched requests in v1.4 SDK.
  Workaround: Upgrade SDK to v2.0 or apply server-side patch (tracked in eng-serving-runtime/known-issues).
- Issue: Intermittent 502 errors when upstream model host scales.
  Workaround: Implement retry with exponential backoff and jitter; configure client to fallback to a smaller capacity model.

Support process and triage flow
------------------------------
- Intake channels: Zendesk (customer portal), email, and CSM routed requests.
- Triage template required fields: customer id, environment (hosted/dedicated/private), reproducible steps, sample request/response, timestamps, and pcap/log links.
- Escalation triggers: repeated 429s >5 minutes, SLO breach, data leakage suspicion, and PII exposure.
- Communication cadence: hourly updates for P1 until mitigation, daily updates for P2 until resolved.

Health checks and QBR materials
------------------------------
Monthly health check (CS -> Customer)
- Items to run: token consumption trend, p95 latency, error rate (5xx/4xx), cost per 1k tokens, cache hit rate, and model regression tests.
- Deliverables: one-page health snapshot and action items.

Quarterly Business Review (QBR) checklist
1. Executive summary: adoption, value delivered, and top 3 wins and risks.
2. Metrics: usage trends, latency, error rates, cost savings from optimization, and model quality metrics (precision, hallucination incidents).
3. Roadmap alignment: upcoming Redwood features and customer ask backlog.
4. Action plan: owners, deadlines, and success metrics.

QBR artifact templates (links)
- Health snapshot template: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/qbr-health-snapshot-template
- Technical appendix: include perf runs, integration test results, and escalation history.

Operational links and runbooks
----------------------------
- Support runbook: /confluence/customer-success-and-support/support-process
- P1 incident playbook: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems
- Performance benchmark suite: /confluence/eng-serving-runtime/benchmarking-and-perf-suite

Appendix A — Communication templates
1. P1 customer-notification (short):
   Subject: Redwood Incident - Service Impact for <customer>
   Body: Short summary, impact, immediate mitigation, ETA for next update, point of contact.
2. Postmortem template: title, timeline, root cause, impact, remediation, owners, and follow-ups.

Appendix B — Onboarding checklist (detailed table)
| Phase | Owner | Deliverables | Target time |
|---|---|---|---:|
| Discovery | CS/SE | Compliance checklist, network requirements | 1 week |
| Integration | SE/Customer | Test harness, perf baseline | 2-4 weeks |
| Validation | CS/SRE | SLA test, canary plan | 1 week |
| Production cutover | CS/Support | Go-live runbook, rollback plan | 2 days |
